title: Inheritance and Shared Actions
summary: A class can build on another class. Think of a bicycle and a bus: both are vehicles, but they move in their own way.
introduction: A class can build on another class. Think of a bicycle and a bus: both are vehicles, but they move in their own way. Read one example at a time. Save it in a .cpp file and use the compiler from the setup lesson to run it.
learningObjectives: Build a child class from a parent class
Replace a shared action with a child action
Use override to check a method name

blocks.text: Inheritance lets a new class reuse parts of another class. Here, a Dog can use the Animal class to get a name.

blocks.title: inheritance-polymorphism.cpp

blocks.text: Give an action a new meaning

A virtual function is an action a child class can replace. The word override asks C++ to check that the action exists in the parent. A destructor cleans up an object. Making it virtual lets cleanup reach the child too when an object is deleted through a parent pointer.

blocks.title: inheritance-polymorphism.cpp

blocks.text: A pure virtual function has = 0. It says that child classes must supply this action before you can make objects from them.

blocks.text: Use inheritance for an "is a" link: a dog is an animal. A dog has a name, so its name should be a field, not a parent class.
